 Hinojosa urges TxDMV to rescind ‘discriminatory’ vehicle registration ID rules before January rollout
 State Sen. Juan Hinojosa, of McAllen, Texas. (Photo credit: Juan Hinojosa's Office) 
 Posted
 Thursday, 
 November 19, 2026 
 9:16 am 
 By Steve Taylor and Daniela Capistran, Reporters 
 McALLEN, Texas — State Sen. Juan “Chuy” Hinojosa of McAllen has formally requested that the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles Board place an action item on its December 10, 2026, agenda to rescind controversial personal identification requirements for vehicle registration before key renewal provisions take effect in the new year.
 In a letter sent to TxDMV Executive Director Daniel Avitia, Hinojosa urged the agency’s governing board to reverse amendments to Title 43 of the Texas Administrative Code (§217.22, §217.26, and §217.29) that were adopted on February 12, 2026.
 Hinojosa noted that the renewal provisions under §217.28 and §217.29 are scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, a change he warned will impact the owners of more than 20 million registered vehicles across Texas.
 “The December 10 meeting is the Board's last scheduled opportunity to act before this happens,” Hinojosa wrote to Avitia. “I urge the Board to take action and rescind these rules.”
 The new regulations limit the types of personal identification documents applicants can present to register or renew a vehicle in Texas—requiring credentials such as a REAL ID-compliant driver’s license, a valid passport, or a Texas handgun license—to verify that an applicant is legally eligible to reside in the state.
 In his letter, Hinojosa argued that the board ignored widespread public and industry pushback when it approved the changes earlier this year. He pointed out that out of 268 formal public comments submitted to the department, 256 opposed the rule changes—including major statewide organizations such as the Tax Assessor-Collectors Association of Texas, the Texas Automobile Dealers Association, the state’s banking and credit union associations, and AARP Texas.
 “These rules are discriminatory, unjust, and lack common sense,” Hinojosa stated. “They transform vehicle registration,whose purpose is to give the state accurate information for every vehicle, into an immigration status check. They fall hardest on residents of border and rural communities, who depend on a vehicle to get to work, school, and medical appointments.”
 Ongoing opposition from Valley lawmakers 
 Hinojosa’s letter is the latest salvo in a year-long battle between Rio Grande Valley lawmakers and state transportation officials over the policy.
 In December 2025, as the agency first began enforcing stricter identification guidance ahead of formal rulemaking, Hinojosa penned a guest column for the Rio Grande Guardian titled, “Hinojosa: State agency’s rule change on registering a vehicle ‘is already creating chaos.’” In that commentary, the McAllen Democrat criticized Avitia and the agency over the administrative shift, warning of confusion and disruption at county tax assessor-collector offices across the state.
 Opposition also mounted in the Texas House ahead of the board’s February vote. On February 11, 2026, state Rep. Terry Canales of Edinburg—chair of the House Select Committee on Transportation Funding—led 46 other Texas House members in sending a joint letter to TxDMV Board Chairman Charles Bacarisse. Presumptive House Speaker Rep. Senfronia Thompson was among the representatives that signed the letter.
 Published in the Rio Grande Guardian under the headline, “House Reps: Texans’ Constitutional rights will be violated under proposed TxDMV rule change,” the letter from the 47 House lawmakers warned that the rule changes overstepped the agency’s statutory authority and risked infringing on Texans’ constitutional rights. The legislators also called on the board to publicly release any supporting data or analysis demonstrating that the stricter ID mandates were necessary to combat fraud in the vehicle registration system.
 Despite the joint letter from the 47 House members and Hinojosa’s own formal public comments submitted on January 5,2026, the TxDMV Board voted to adopt the amendments on February 12, with initial provisions taking effect in March and the broader registration renewal mandates set to begin January 1, 2027.
 Full Text of Sen. Hinojosa’s Letter 
 Here is the full text of Sen. Hinojosa’s letter to TxDMV Executive Director Daniel Avitia:
 Dear Mr. Avitia,
 I write to formally request that an action item be added to the agenda for December 10, 2026 meeting of the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles Board to rescind the amendments to 43 TAC §217.22, §217.26, and §217.29, relating to personal identification requirements for vehicle registration, which the Board adopted on February 12, 2026.
 I was disappointed by the board's decision in February to move forward with these rules. On January 5, 2026, I submitted formal public comment urging the board not to adopt them, and I was not alone. Of the 268 comments the department received, 256 opposed the rules, including the Tax Assessor-Collectors Association of Texas, the Texas Automobile Dealers Association, the state's banking and credit union association, AARP Texas, and many others. The Board chose to disregard that overwhelming opposition.
 These rules are discriminatory, unjust, and lack common sense. They transform vehicle registration, whose purpose is to give the state accurate information for every vehicle, into an immigration status check. They fall hardest on residents of border and rural communities, who depend on a vehicle to get to work, school, and medical appointments. The Board still has an opportunity to cure this. The renewal provisions in §217.28, and §217.29 take effect January 1, 2027, and will impact the owners of more than 20 million registered vehicles. The December 10 meeting is the Board's last scheduled opportunity to act before this happens. I urge the Board to take action and rescind these rules.
